feed.title: AI · Agents & Infrastructure — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: A hand-curated, annotated link directory across ten areas, from software and AI to security, economics and architecture. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Awesome Claude Code
entry.content:
A resource list for Claude Code, Anthropic’s terminal-based coding assistant. Unlike the official docs, it gathers community-shared slash commands, hooks and CLAUDE.md examples.

https://github.com/hesreallyhim/awesome-claude-code

entry.title: Awesome Copilot Agents
entry.content:
A resource list of agents for Copilot, GitHub’s AI pair-programming assistant. Unlike general Copilot tips, it focuses on ready agent definitions and custom instruction files.

https://github.com/Code-and-Sorts/awesome-copilot-agents

entry.title: Awesome Firebase Genkit
entry.content:
A resource list for Genkit, the open-source framework for building AI-powered features. Unlike frameworks such as LangChain, it integrates tightly with Firebase and Google Cloud and ships a local developer UI.

https://github.com/xavidop/awesome-firebase-genkit

entry.title: Awesome Gemini CLI
entry.content:
A resource list for Gemini CLI, Google’s terminal-based coding assistant. Unlike Claude Code lists, it gathers extensions, MCP configurations and workflows specific to Google’s tool.

https://github.com/Piebald-AI/awesome-gemini-cli

entry.title: Bernstein
entry.content:
An open-source governance layer for AI agents that enforces rules and limits on what agents may do. Unlike agent frameworks it is about control: it does not build the agent, it constrains a built agent’s actions with policy and logs them.

https://github.com/sipyourdrink-ltd/bernstein

entry.title: Tongyi DeepResearch
entry.content:
Alibaba’s open-source “deep research” agent model that runs multi-step web research on its own. Unlike chat LLMs it is an agent: rather than a single reply it calls tools and browses sources to carry a long research task from start to finish.

https://github.com/Alibaba-NLP/DeepResearch

entry.title: PromptLayer
entry.content:
A platform for versioning, logging and evaluating LLM prompts, so you can trace which prompt produced which output. Unlike general APM tooling it treats the prompt as a first-class object, separating prompt changes from code deploys.

https://promptlayer.com/

entry.title: whisper.cpp
entry.content:
A dependency-free C/C++ port of OpenAI’s Whisper speech recognition model that runs at a reasonable pace even on CPU. Against the Python original there is no install burden and it compiles to a single binary — small enough for embedded targets.

https://github.com/ggml-org/whisper.cpp

entry.title: last30days
entry.content:
A skill sweeping the last thirty days of Reddit, X and YouTube on a topic. Unlike a general web search it focuses only on recent community discussion — aimed at the gap between a model’s training cutoff and today.

https://github.com/mvanhorn/last30days-skill

entry.title: Agno
entry.content:
An agent framework with memory, tools and knowledge base built into the core. Unlike frameworks such as LangChain there is no extra abstraction layer: agent instantiation lands in the microsecond range, which keeps it light with many agents.

https://www.agno.com/

entry.title: Arize Phoenix
entry.content:
An LLM tracing and evaluation tool that runs inside a notebook and renders traces locally. Unlike tracing tools that need a server, it stays local and visualises the embedding space, so you find the source of a retrieval failure by looking at clustering.

https://phoenix.arize.com/

entry.title: AWS Bedrock Agents
entry.content:
Agent definition, tool schema and knowledge base are configured in the AWS console, and AWS runs the runtime. Unlike self-operated frameworks such as LangGraph there is no infrastructure to run; the price is fitting the flow into AWS’s shape.

https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/agents/

entry.title: AWS Bedrock Guardrails
entry.content:
Content filters, denied-topic lists and PII redaction. Unlike libraries you run yourself such as NeMo Guardrails it is a managed service, and it can be applied as a standalone API to models outside Bedrock too.

https://aws.amazon.com/bedrock/guardrails/

entry.title: AWS Strands Agents
entry.content:
AWS’s open-source agent SDK. Unlike frameworks such as LangGraph where you wire the flow, you hand the model a tool list and let it plan; less code to write, at the cost of harder tracing when you need to see where a decision came from.

https://strandsagents.com/

entry.title: Azure AI Content Safety
entry.content:
A classifier scoring text and images across four harm categories with severity levels. You set the thresholds yourself — an alternative to training your own moderation model.

https://azure.microsoft.com/products/ai-services/ai-content-safety

entry.title: Azure AI Foundry
entry.content:
Model catalogue, agent service, evaluation and content filtering in one portal. Rather than assembling these from separate services, it offers a stack gathered for enterprise deployments that need compliance and region control.

https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/ai-foundry/

entry.title: Azure OpenAI Service
entry.content:
OpenAI models with Azure’s region selection and private networking. Unlike OpenAI’s own API you gain that compliance; the price is that new model versions arrive here later.

https://learn.microsoft.com/azure/ai-services/openai/

entry.title: CAMEL-AI
entry.content:
A research framework for societies of role-playing agents steering each other. Suited to scaled experiments and synthetic data generation, not to production plumbing.

https://www.camel-ai.org/

entry.title: Composio
entry.content:
Ships ready tool definitions and delegated OAuth for a thousand-odd apps. Instead of writing auth per SaaS, you hand the authorisation off to it.

https://composio.dev/

entry.title: CrewAI
entry.content:
You give each agent a role, goal and backstory; tasks are dispatched sequentially or hierarchically. Conceptually simple, but it gives less fine control over flow than LangGraph.

https://www.crewai.com/

entry.title: DSPy
entry.content:
You do not write prompt text — you declare input/output signatures and supply examples, and an optimiser generates the prompts and few-shot demonstrations. Unlike prompt-template frameworks, it hands prompt tuning to a compiler.

https://dspy.ai/

entry.title: FastMCP
entry.content:
Decorate a function and it becomes an MCP tool, with the schema derived from type hints. Unlike the raw official SDK, it erases nearly all the boilerplate you would hand-write.

https://gofastmcp.com/

entry.title: GitHub MCP Server
entry.content:
The official server exposing repo, issue, PR and Actions operations as tools. Unlike community servers it is maintained by GitHub itself, with fine-grained permission scopes, so you can hand an assistant read-only access.

https://github.com/github/github-mcp-server

entry.title: Guardrails AI
entry.content:
Runs output through a chain of schemas and validators, retrying or repairing on failure. Unlike NeMo Guardrails, which governs the dialogue flow, it polices the shape and content of the generated text.

https://www.guardrailsai.com/

entry.title: Helicone
entry.content:
An LLM observability tool: change the base URL and requests are logged as they pass through. Unlike tracers that need SDK integration it works as a proxy, so it bolts onto an existing project without code changes.

https://www.helicone.ai/

entry.title: Lakera Guard
entry.content:
An API focused on prompt injection and jailbreak detection. Unlike general content filters, it is fed by real attack data harvested from its gamified Gandalf experiment.

https://www.lakera.ai/

entry.title: LangChain
entry.content:
Wraps model, vector store and tool providers behind common interfaces. Compared with thinner frameworks its strongest card is the integration count; the thickness of the abstraction layer is the most frequent complaint.

https://www.langchain.com/

entry.title: LangChain Agents (öğretici)
entry.content:
The official walkthrough of defining tools, binding a model and wiring the loop. Unlike conceptual explainers it proceeds in running code — the shortest way to see how the tool-calling protocol actually works.

https://python.langchain.com/docs/tutorials/agents/

entry.title: Langfuse
entry.content:
Framework-agnostic LLM tracing and evaluation, OpenTelemetry-compatible. Unlike hosted services such as LangSmith you can self-host it, so prompt and response data never leaves your infrastructure.

https://langfuse.com/

entry.title: LangSmith
entry.content:
Shows input, output, latency and token count for every chain step separately. Not tied to LangChain, though that is where the integration is tightest.

https://smith.langchain.com/

entry.title: LlamaIndex Workflows
entry.content:
An async runtime where steps emit and listen for events. Instead of building a graph you mark functions with `@step`, and parallel branches fall out naturally.

https://docs.llamaindex.ai/en/stable/module_guides/workflow/

entry.title: MCP Registry
entry.content:
The official MCP server registry. Rather than scattered GitHub lists, it offers one machine-readable source, which lets clients automate installation.

https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/

entry.title: MCP Sunucu Koleksiyonu
entry.content:
Reference MCP servers for tools such as filesystem, Git and fetch. Unlike third-party servers in the registry, these are written by the protocol’s authors as examples — a quick read before writing your own.

https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers

entry.title: Microsoft Agent Framework
entry.content:
The new line merging AutoGen’s experimental side with Semantic Kernel’s enterprise side. Unlike either one alone it combines both, and arrives pre-wired to Azure identity and monitoring.

https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/agent-framework/

entry.title: Microsoft AutoGen
entry.content:
Agents solve tasks by talking in a group chat, with a manager agent deciding who speaks next. Unlike graph-based frameworks such as LangGraph the flow is a conversation; research-rooted, so the API can shift sharply between versions.

https://microsoft.github.io/autogen/

entry.title: Microsoft Presidio
entry.content:
Detects and redacts personal data — national IDs, IBANs, emails — in text and images, with customisable recognisers. Unlike cloud PII services it is open source and runs locally — for the anonymisation step before data reaches a model.

https://microsoft.github.io/presidio/

entry.title: Model Context Protocol
entry.content:
An open protocol over JSON-RPC for exposing tools and data sources to models. Unlike writing a plugin per model, you write the server once and any MCP-speaking client can use it.

https://modelcontextprotocol.io/

entry.title: NeMo Guardrails
entry.content:
You declare permitted conversation flows in a DSL called Colang. The control sits in the dialogue’s trajectory rather than the output text, cutting topic drift at the entrance.

https://github.com/NVIDIA/NeMo-Guardrails

entry.title: OpenAI Agents SDK
entry.content:
Settles for four concepts: agents, tools, handoffs and guardrails, with tracing built in. Compared with frameworks such as LangGraph, the learning curve is far shallower.

https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/

entry.title: Prisma AIRS (Protect AI)
entry.content:
Scans model files for malicious payloads — because pickle deserialisation can execute arbitrary code, a downloaded checkpoint is a real attack surface. Unlike classic malware scanners it understands these model formats; Protect AI joined Palo Alto Networks in 2025 and the product now lives under Prisma AIRS.

https://protectai.com/
